sites.name: Tam Dao Tourist Area
sites.event: Known as the 'Da Lat of the North', it was once a luxury resort of the French in the early 20th century.

sites.name: Tay Thien Scenic Area
sites.event: One of the oldest Buddhist and Mother Goddess worship (worshiping National Mother Tay Thien Lang Thi Tieu) centers in Northern Vietnam.

sites.name: Binh Son Tower
sites.event: The tallest and most beautiful terracotta tower remaining from the Tran Dynasty (14th century), a unique architectural and artistic monument.

sites.name: Dai Lai Lake
sites.event: A vast artificial lake located at the foot of Ngoc Thanh Mountain, famous for its picturesque landscapes and resorts.

sites.name: Huong Canh Pottery Village
sites.event: A traditional craft village famous for its earthenware products and highly waterproof jars, associated with the history of fighting the Ming invaders.

sites.name: Truc Lam Tay Thien Zen Monastery
sites.event: One of the three largest Zen monasteries of the Truc Lam Yen Tu Zen sect in Vietnam, located halfway up Thach Ban Mountain.

sites.name: Dam Vac
sites.event: A vast natural lagoon likened to the 'West Lake' of Vinh Yen, providing an abundant source of seafood (tep Dau Dam Vac).

sites.name: Tho Tang Communal House
sites.event: An ancient 17th-century communal house with the most exquisite wood carving art, testifying to the prosperity of an ancient trading land.

sites.name: Dong Dau Archaeological Site
sites.event: An important site proving the continuous development of ancient Vietnamese from the Bronze Age to the Iron Age (from Phung Nguyen to Dong Son culture).

sites.name: Temple of Left Chancellor Tran Nguyen Han
sites.event: The place of worship for the famous general who made great contributions to the Lam Son Uprising, with the temple built by the people on the site of his former home.

sites.name: Tam Dao Silver Waterfall
sites.event: A beautiful waterfall hidden in the mountains and forests of Tam Dao, with water flowing as white as silver.

sites.name: Huong Canh Communal House Complex
sites.event: Consisting of 3 communal houses (Huong Canh, Tien Canh, Ngoc Canh) famous for their unique folk wood carving architecture from the Later Le Dynasty.
